waves.overlap_evidence: Michigan, Tennessee, and Massachusetts agents were active while the root Arizona workstream inspected official sources.

candidate.publisher: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, Corporations Division
candidate.availability: possible written customized listing under FY2026 enabling authority; no published bulk product, API, recurring delivery contract, or current machine schema
candidate.price: Unknown; LARA may quote a reasonable fee plus applicable production or FOIA costs

observed_evidence: Michigan's FY2026 budget permits otherwise-unavailable customized nonconfidential listings for a reasonable fee but does not define a bulk product or contract.

The current MiBusiness Registry Portal is an interactive search; the legacy COFS service was retired and Michigan website terms prohibit automated access and commercial resale without written authorization.
An official October 2025 aggregate reports about 1.18 million favorable-status entities, but it is neither a current row count nor an extract contract.
The Division-assigned nine-digit identifier is only a candidate key because current extract presence, immutability, non-reuse, and migration lifecycle are undocumented.
Registry standing reflects legal filing condition and does not prove an operating business or physical establishment; registered offices may be resident-agent locations.
required_exclusions: resident and registered agents and every registered-office or service address
incorporators, organizers, officers, directors, members, managers, partners, owners and their addresses
email, phone, signature and filer-contact fields
FEIN, SSN, tax, payment, banking and non-registry government identifiers; preserve the public Division ID
filing images, documents and narrative or free-text fields
states.strongest_bounded_next_action: Ask the Michigan Corporations Division whether a recurring person-free entity extract exists and request only its blank agreement, price sheet, schema, aggregate size, identifier/status/address dictionaries, delivery and change contract, automation authorization, and written downstream-use rights. Do not submit a record request, access the portal programmatically, pay, or implement a connector first.

candidate.publisher: Tennessee Secretary of State, Division of Business and Charitable Organizations
candidate.availability: official user-directed purchase and download; no public current price, order contract, subscription, anonymous file route, API, or recurring-delivery specification
candidate.price: Unknown; current database price and service fees are not published

observed_evidence: The Secretary of State advertises purchase and download of a Business Entity Database through TNCaB but publishes no current machine or delivery contract.
An official Q4 2024 report states 406,667 active entities; that historical aggregate does not establish current database population, history scope, or bytes.
The SOS control number is the candidate key, but uniqueness, non-reuse, conversion, merger, reinstatement and migration continuity are undocumented.
Tennessee Revenue states that inactive, administratively dissolved or revoked entities may still conduct business, so registry status cannot become an operating-status assertion.
Official forms distinguish principal office, mailing address, and registered agent or office, while the database schema and privacy-safe projection remain unpublished.
required_exclusions: registered agents, registered offices and service addresses
officers, directors, managers, members, partners, organizers, incorporators, signers and their addresses
email, phone, signature and direct-contact fields
FEIN, SSN, tax, payment, banking and non-registry government identifiers; preserve the public SOS control number
filing images, documents and narrative or free-text fields
states.strongest_bounded_next_action: Ask Tennessee SOS for the current unsigned database-download terms, exact price, schema-only header or person-free sample, entity and status dictionaries, control-number lifecycle, address roles, current aggregate size, delivery/change/checksum contract, automation support, and written downstream-use rights. Do not purchase, obtain credentials, request rows, or implement a connector first.

candidate.publisher: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth, Corporations Division
candidate.product: Corporations Information Management System full extract
candidate.availability: paid extract available monthly in weekly increments; data elements and file layout are supplied only by the filing office on request
candidate.price: $4,800 per year or $100 per week; filing images are extra and excluded

observed_evidence: 950 CMR 113.15 establishes the price and monthly-in-weekly-increments cadence but says data elements and layout are available only on request.
Official registry descriptions span corporations, nonprofits, LLCs, partnerships and other legal forms, but the paid extract's exact type, history and active-only scope is unpublished.
Public search exposes separate nine-digit Identification Number and Filing Number fields without an extract-presence or lifecycle guarantee.
Good standing is an administrative filing condition rather than proof of current operation, and registered office, principal office and person-linked addresses have distinct roles.
Official website terms prohibit scraping and derivative use of the search surface; unattended paid-bulk transport and downstream product rights are undocumented.
required_exclusions: registered agents, registered offices and service addresses
officers, directors, managers, signers, authorized persons and their addresses
email, phone, signature and direct-contact fields

Do not purchase, search or scrape the portal, request rows, or implement a connector first.

candidate.availability: paid full database as double-quote-delimited CSV by CD-ROM or download, or partial extraction by CD-ROM or email, after a signed purpose statement; custom requests may be denied or additionally priced
candidate.price: $1,000 full database or $75 partial extraction; commercial-use and current public-record fees may also apply

observed_evidence: The Commission advertises full and partial database extractions, but delivery requires a signed request and payment rather than an anonymous public bulk route.
The form offers double-quote-delimited comma-separated data and high-level field groups, but no exact current header, type contract, encoding, sample, row count, bytes, or checksum.
The request form lists only high-level business name and address, date, agent or officer, status, domicile and business-type groups; it provides no public stable-identifier contract.
Arizona law and the request form require disclosure of commercial purpose and allow purpose-specific pricing, denial for misuse, and restrictions on use beyond the stated purpose.
The Arizona Business Center replaced eCorp in January 2026, adding a migration boundary whose effects on schema, identifiers and recurring extracts are undocumented.
